q: What is Gamble With Your Friends?
a: A 1–6 player online co-op game on Steam where the crew shares one bank account and has five minutes a day to hit a loan shark’s quota. TEAM GWYF developed it, TENSTACK published it, and it released on 1 May 2026. It is not real-money gambling.

q: Is it called Gamble With Friends?
a: No. The Steam title is Gamble With Your Friends, AppID 3892270. “Gamble With Friends” is a common search miss. This wiki covers that game only.

q: How much does Gamble With Your Friends cost?
a: The US Steam store API on 18 Oct 2026 listed $7.99, on sale at $4.95 (−38%). Sales end. Check the store page for today’s price.

q: Can you play Gamble With Your Friends solo?
a: Yes. The store page and the developer FAQ both say solo is possible and not recommended. There is no matchmaking. Multiplayer is Steam friends only, up to six people in a lobby.

V1.0.30’s patch notes say Endless Mode stops you seeing the ending and blocks the achievements tied to the different endings. It is a per-save toggle on an empty slot, and it locks once the save is created. Floor achievements are a separate question; the notes do not say Endless blocks those.

q: Is Gamble With Your Friends on PS5, Xbox, or Switch?
a: No. The Steam store lists Windows only, and the developer FAQ says they are only supporting Windows PCs for now. It is not a social poker app, and it is not cross-platform with a console casino.

q: Does it run on Steam Deck?
a: Unverified. There is no Mac or Linux build on the store page, and no Proton rating is cited here. Treat Deck as unsupported until you test it.

q: How many players, and how do I join a friend?
a: 1–6, friends only. The host creates a lobby and sends a fresh Steam invite. If someone cannot join, turn VPNs off and read the online fix page. Do not download a third-party “online fix.”

For anything tied to a floor, you almost certainly skipped the Phone Booth challenge or accepted a different one. That is the first check. A current list of still-bugged achievements was not verified for V1.0.30, so this site does not name one.

Three, all on day 13: pay the debt, win Double or Nothing, or lose Double or Nothing. The launch coin-flip achievements are not endings. You can take all three ending achievements from one late save if you quit the moment each one pops.
No. You buy the game on Steam. The cash, tickets, and debt are fictional. The publisher’s store text says they do not condone gambling.

q: What is the peak player count?
a: Not listed here. Third-party charts disagree, and a peak was not taken from Steam for this page. The developer did announce 1,000,000+ copies in the first week and 2,000,000+ copies in the first month.

q: Can I turn off the 5-minute timer?
a: Yes, before the save exists. V1.0.30 added a cogwheel on an empty slot for timer on/off, timer length, difficulty, starting money, starting tickets, and Endless Mode. Those choices lock when the slot is created.
